title: Cordless Electric Kettles With Auto Shut-Off: What They Do and What They Don't
subtitle: What a cordless kettle with auto shut-off does, what to check before buying, and the limits to keep in mind.
excerpt: A cordless electric kettle with auto shut-off stops heating once the water boils, but it still means lifting and pouring hot water. Here is how these kettles work, what to look for if lifting is hard, and what the shut-off cannot do.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: For many of us, the day starts with a cup of tea or instant coffee. A stovetop kettle does the job, but it asks you to keep track of a burner and to lift a heavy pot of hot water.

A cordless electric kettle with auto shut-off is one alternative. It heats water on its own base, stops heating when the water boils, and lifts off the base so you can pour without a cord attached. It is not risk-free, and it still needs your attention, but it can be a simple option for a countertop kitchen routine.

The kettle sits on a flat base that plugs into the wall. When you lift the kettle off, no cord comes with it, which is what "cordless" means here. You fill it, set it back on the base, and switch it on.

Auto shut-off means the kettle stops heating once the water boils. A separate feature called boil-dry protection is meant to protect the kettle if it is switched on without enough water. These are two different features, so confirm that a kettle lists both.

Some kettles also offer preset temperatures and a keep-warm setting. For example, Consumer Reports lists the Breville IQ Kettle with five preset temperatures, a 20-minute keep-warm, auto shut-off and boil-dry protection.

Auto shut-off only ends the heating. It is not a cooking safety device, and it does not replace paying attention around a hot kettle. It does not stop splashes or protect you from a scald when pouring. Going cordless also does not make the kettle lighter: lifting it off the base still means lifting all the water inside. If someone cannot handle hot water at all, or needs a kettle that pours without any lifting, this is not the right gadget.

items: Both safety features: look for auto shut-off and boil-dry protection listed by name on the maker's page.

Weight and handle: a full 1.7-liter kettle is heavy. Check the empty weight on the seller's listing and think about how the handle will sit in your hand. If your hands are stiff or painful, ask your doctor or an occupational therapist what is safe for you to lift.
Water-level window: some kettles have one, so you can see how much water is inside. Filling less means lifting less.

Spout and lid: NBC News Select reports that "When shopping for an electric kettle, experts recommended looking at temperature control features, materials and the spout." Whichever kettle you pick, make sure you can grip the spout and lid comfortably.
Controls: look at which switches and lights the kettle has, and whether you would be comfortable using them. Preset temperatures are optional.
Warranty and returns: Consumer Reports lists a 1-year limited warranty for the Breville IQ. Warranty terms vary by maker, so read the warranty and the store's return window before you buy.
Costs: we found no monthly fees listed for these kettles, but check the seller's page for the price and any extras.

sections.content: Setting It Up and Using It Well
Pick a spot on the counter near an outlet, with room to set your mug right beside the kettle. That way you pour a short distance instead of carrying hot water across the kitchen.
Fill the kettle at the sink before setting it on the base. A full kettle is the heaviest it will ever be, so fill only as much as you need. Make sure the lid is closed before you switch it on.

Watch the first few boils from nearby to confirm the kettle shuts itself off. One customer review we came across for the Hamilton Beach 40880 said its auto shut-off did not work. That is a single report, but it is a good reason to test the kettle early. If it does not shut off, unplug it, stop using it and contact the store or maker.

If you are buying for a parent, check the store's return window before you buy, since we have not confirmed one for the Hamilton Beach. Keep the box and receipt until you are sure. When it arrives, have them lift and pour a partly filled kettle. If it feels awkward or heavy, a different model may suit them better. If stiff or painful hands make this hard, a doctor or occupational therapist can advise.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: A cordless kettle with auto shut-off will not do everything, but it can be a useful part of a morning routine. Choose one that feels comfortable in the hand, fill it lightly, and enjoy your tea.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 40880 Stainless Steel 1.7 L Kettle
products.blurb: Suits someone who wants a cord-free kettle with an on/off switch and a power light. The maker lists auto shutoff with boil-dry protection, a water-level window and a drip-free spout, with a 1.7-liter (7.2-cup) capacity.

products.blurb: Suits tea drinkers who want temperature choices. Consumer Reports lists five preset temperatures, a 20-minute keep-warm, auto shut-off, boil-dry protection and a 1-year limited warranty.
